meta.title: Design cookbook — interfaces that coordinate humans with generative models

method.derivation: grounded-theory open coding on a 200-paper stratified sample, saturated at paradigm level by n~100
method.axis: 28-candidate seed (10 corpus-derived problems + 8 PI-named constructs + 10 scan constructs) merged abductively into 18 categories
method.naming: every paradigm, sub-paradigm and difficulty name is a term harvested from the corpus or supplied by the PI; zero analyst coinages

caveats: papers[] holds the 1,651 papers that were assigned a design paradigm. The other 97 of the 1,748-paper corpus were read and coded but fit no paradigm; they are in excluded_papers[] with reasons, not omitted. See meta.corpus_accounting. The 2 orphan PDFs (9767, 9769) both received a paradigm and are in papers[] with an empty url field, not in excluded_papers[].

Lifecycle stage assignment is the PI's, as given. lifecycle.proposed_adjustments holds 7 rows: 6 propose an evidence-backed change and 1 (P11) records that no change is needed. NONE are applied. lifecycle_adjusted.png renders 5 of the 6 — P13's is conditional (either/or, see its note) and was left unapplied.
Sub-paradigm v1.1 split proposals for P6/P8/P10/P11 are recorded but not applied.
Five difficulty names rest on 3-5 paper attestation and carry higher-frequency alternates.
F1 keeps the PI term "gulf of envisioning" though it appears in only 6 of its 415 papers; corpus alternative is "articulate" (105).
284 papers sit in per-paradigm tails below the sub-paradigm promotion bar; 219 of them carry cross-cutting patterns instead.

Sub-paradigm counts are per-paper assignments. Eight watch-list sub-paradigms differ from the original aggregate clustering (largest: P6 Structured Format 145->115, P10 Role-Playing Agent 40->59); both numbers are carried as n and n_aggregate_cluster. The per-paper count is authoritative and matches paper_rids.

3 coded papers carry no primary difficulty (2 genuine no-fit, 1 parse failure); they appear in papers[] and in paradigm rid lists but not in matrix cells, so matrix rows carry both n (papers) and n_with_factor (papers in cells). Listed in unassigned_papers.

corpus_accounting.reconciliation: 1,748 PDFs were all read and coded. 1,651 were assigned a design paradigm and appear in papers[]. 97 fit no paradigm and appear in excluded_papers[] with the reason. 1,651 + 97 = 1,748. Nothing was dropped or left unread.
corpus_accounting.interpretation: The no-fit residue is overwhelmingly papers that present no designed interactive artifact — empirical studies, frameworks, elicitations, toolkits, datasets. 87 of the 97 were independently flagged scope-doubt during coding. Open-coding all 97 produced no cluster reaching the promotion bar, so this is evidence the taxonomy held, not that it missed a paradigm. Screening, not the taxonomy, is where these entered.

orphan_disposition.note: The 2 orphan PDFs have no manifest row (no venue/title/DOI) but were coded and both received a paradigm, so they are in papers[] with an empty url — the only papers[] records without a working link.

no_fit_artifact_breakdown.note: Cross-cutting count, not a sum of whole contribution kinds. Per-kind: framework_or_theory 11/11, elicitation_or_probe 11/11, empirical_study 30/42, toolkit_or_infrastructure 4/7, interactive_system 0/15, method_or_algorithm 5/7, dataset_or_benchmark 1/1, unclassified 3/3. Per-paper truth is the presents_interactive_artifact field on each excluded_papers[] record.

proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Split across stages: keep Likeness-of-a-Real-Individual (23) in 2.5 Personalization; move Assistant-as-Character (77) and Roleplay Counterpart (40) to 2.2 During AI working; move Population Surrogate Panel (26) to 2.3 Eval
proposed_adjustments.evidence: Only 23/183 (13%) of P10 is personalization in the conditioning sense. Top problems are H7 reciprocal feedback 27%, H6 motivation 19%, H8 skill rehearsal 18% — none is a personalization signature. The 4 sub-clusters come from the approved watch-list analysis (kappa 0.75).

proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Add to 2.2 During AI working for the Implicit Signal Conditioning sub-cluster (35 papers); keep the other 212 in 2.1
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P6's Implicit Signal Conditioning harvests signals (gaze, speech features, learning-analytics data) at generation time rather than being set beforehand, so it is not context-setting in the elicitation sense.

P3 Context-Triggered Proactive Assistance n=124; H4 workflow interruption is its #2 problem at 20% (26 papers). Triggering on ambient context IS context acquisition — currently the only paradigm in 2.2 with no 2.1 membership despite 'Context-Triggered' in its name.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Pipeline of Stages with Iterative Refinement
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P5 n=310, the largest paradigm. H1 opacity is its #2 problem at 11% (37 papers) — inspectable intermediate stages are what the user watches DURING generation, not only what they steer afterwards.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Explanation and Verification of Generated Content
proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Drop 2.2 During AI working, keep 2.3 only — OR keep both if in-generation self-check counts
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P13 n=67 is 55% H1 opacity, 19% H5 prediction blind spots. Verification overlays act on already-generated content; whether that is 'during' depends on whether streaming self-check counts as in-flight. Sam's call.
proposed_adjustments.note: Stated as either/or — depends on whether in-generation self-check counts as "during". Left at 2.2+2.3 in lifecycle_adjusted.png pending the PI's call.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Adaptive Interfaces from Inferred User State
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P15 n=29 is 31% H1 opacity, 13% H4 workflow interruption. Inferred-state adaptation happens continuously at runtime; the watch-list analysis kept it whole as 'Inferred-State Continuous Adaptation' — continuous means in-flight.
P11 n=37 is 35% H10 social friction. Its AI-Mediated Human Hand-Off sub-cluster (18) is turn-sequencing, which is both setup and follow-up. Assignment already reflects that.

P1.name: Traceability to Sources
P1.definition: Establishes a persistent, addressable link between a generated artifact (a sentence, glyph, chat turn, or graph node) and the specific source unit it was derived from, so that selecting one side highlights, scrolls to, or edits the other.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Ground every generated claim or explanation in retrievable, cited source material rather than free generation.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Users cannot trust or verify AI outputs that float free of checkable evidence.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Restricts answerable scope to what retrieved/vetted evidence covers, limiting creative or broad responses.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 15815: grounds AI-generated responses to the posts of the Kaggle community; 9086: Ground guidance in curated sources and attach citations in a struc- tured manner.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Synchronize selection or hover across paired representations so interacting with one highlights the corresponding element in the other.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Readers cannot otherwise tell which chart, code, or diagram element a given text or answer refers to.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Simultaneously highlighting many correspondences clutters the display and hurts readability.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 8598: when the reader hovers over a phrase in the summary text, corresponding passages in the so; 13531: ensures that the same entities are matched across diferent text and diagrams, allowing for

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Expose the AI's generation process as an explicit intermediate structured representation (graph, pipeline, tuple) before the final output.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Hidden reasoning inside a single answer or line of code prevents users from inspecting how it was derived.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Showing full intermediate structure risks overwhelming users who just wanted the answer.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 10427: Sop = [op1, op2, ..., opn] ←Decompose(qx, sx); 13743: Before each LLM response, the system generates an LLM understanding graph in Panel B

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Keep the original, raw source content visible and accessible alongside generated or derived content rather than replacing it.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Users need to verify automated summaries or drafts against the material they were built from.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Conflicts with collapsing or hiding content by default to reduce clutter and cognitive load.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 10014: the original data, NL code and results of computations were always visible on the Grid; 17002: the system incorporates plain language alongside original paper content

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Let users directly edit the intermediate structured representation instead of only accepting or rejecting the final output.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Small errors in an automated pipeline otherwise force users to redo or re-describe the whole task.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Requires users to understand a structure well enough to correct it, and edits must propagate consistently.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 10427: users are allowed to edit (i.e., add, delete, modify) the operations in Sop; 13743: Instead of rewrit- ing everything, I just fixed the node that was wrong and got what I wan

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Visually mark content by provenance (AI-generated vs. human-written vs. copied) with distinct, in-place encoding rather than a uniform blend.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Readers and writers otherwise cannot tell at a glance which parts of a text or code file came from whom.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Adds persistent visual marks that can clutter the reading or writing surface.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 2937: The system highlights text written (orange) and infuenced (green) by the AI.; 2881: keeping track of the provenance of each part of the code, including code that has been AI-

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Signal absent or uncertain grounding explicitly (unsure labels, missing-value flags, unlinked phrases) rather than fabricating or silently omitting a link.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Users trust unmarked silence as confirmation, so unflagged gaps in evidence go unnoticed and mislead.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Biasing toward flagging more (recall over precision) raises false-positive noise that erodes trust in flags.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 8598: A hallucinated phrase will either not be highlighted in the first place; 8732: Missing information, such as the dosage for an advised drug, was flagged with a question m

P2.name: Generating Multiple Alternatives for Comparison
P2.definition: Produces several parallel candidate outputs, framings, or branches for the same request or decision point, then lays them out together so the user can inspect, filter, cluster, or rank across them and pick or combine rather than receive

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Generate and present multiple candidate outputs together instead of committing to a single result.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Builders default to producing one best answer; deliberately branching or co-displaying alternatives requires added generation and layout logic.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Trades against simplicity and reduced cognitive/screen load of a single definitive output.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 2325: showing four LLMs’ responses side-by-side to the same prompt; 2415: the grid lay­ out is specifcally inspired from text-to-image generation “style guidelines”

subparadigms.name: Multiple Suggestions Shown Together
subparadigms.definition: This mechanism generates multiple candidate outputs in parallel from a shared prompt, template, or query and presents them together without imposing similarity clustering, aligned annotation, or branch structure. The comparison surface is a flat, unordered or independently-ranked set—grid, list, carousel, or side-by-side panels—where each candidate is addressable individually rather than through inter-candidate relationships.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If candidates are positioned or grouped by embedding/feature similarity to reveal a coverage or diversity structure among them, it is Similarity-positioned candidate space, not this; here candidates sit in fixed slots (grid/list/carousel) with no similarity-derived layout.

principles.principle: Generate the candidate set from multiple independent models, pipelines, or personas rather than one generator.
principles.rationale: A single generator repeats its own biases, giving users a falsely narrow range to judge from.
principles.tension: Adds engineering complexity and cost compared to running one generation pipeline.
principles.evidence: 4917: AP1: prompt with one-shot example, AP2: prompt to audio, then pat­ tern, AP3: real finger–; 5554: Ten specialized storyteller personas independently generate diverse narrative possibilitie

principles.principle: Let users select exactly one candidate from the set to adopt and refine further.
principles.rationale: Users need a clear way to commit and build on one option instead of juggling many at once.
principles.tension: Trades against keeping all candidates equally available for ongoing comparison.
principles.evidence: 8543: allows users to select one enhanced result (e.g., 2/16 options) for refinement (3), enabli; 5554: The human user evaluates, selects, and optionally edits the most promising beat from the g

principles.principle: Require an explicit user action to trigger candidate generation rather than surfacing suggestions automatically.
principles.rationale: Unsolicited AI suggestions interrupt focus and erode users' sense of control over their own work.
principles.tension: Conflicts with proactively surfacing many candidates to widen exploration.
principles.evidence: 2002: We also use this design with an explicit request key to better understand how and when use; 8404: allows users to write stories and request suggestions by selecting a text snippet and clic

principles.principle: Let users individually favorite, star, vote, or bookmark candidates to record preference.
principles.rationale: Users need a lightweight way to mark promising options without committing immediately amid many choices.
principles.tension: Adds interaction overhead compared to simply picking one candidate outright.
principles.evidence: 10157: Searchers can bookmark the current best image seen during the search session; 4534: click “Star” to favorite a reading material under the relevant context or click “Delete”

principles.principle: Attach automatic quality scores or metrics to each candidate to support comparison.
principles.rationale: Users struggle to judge many similar-looking candidates without objective criteria to differentiate them.
principles.tension: Risks users over-trusting scores instead of exercising their own judgment.
principles.evidence: 12795: a multi-view hybrid scoring approach that leverages MLLMs with innovative high-level metri; 2714: automatically evaluates these outputs to compare how each prompt performed on each criteri

subparadigms.name: Similarity Clustering in a Design Space
subparadigms.definition: This mechanism generates a batch of candidate outputs and positions each one in a similarity-derived space (embedding, feature, or property axis) so that proximity encodes how alike candidates are to each other. The comparison surface is a continuous or clustered spatial layout — 2D canvases, bubble maps, axis projections, or thumbnail groupings — where location and distance, not fixed slots, carry the comparative meaning.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If candidates are arranged by computed similarity/distance (position or cluster membership is meaningful), it is this sub-paradigm; if candidates instead fill a fixed grid or parallel slot set with no similarity-derived positioning, it is Flat co-present candidate set.

principles.principle: Let users steer further candidate generation via natural-language or direct interactive input.
principles.rationale: Fixed sliders or presets can't capture the nuanced intent users have for refining results.
principles.tension: Conflicts with automatically diversifying generation into areas the user didn't request.
principles.evidence: 4876: Generate additional variations to explore by providing an optional grounding instruction; 5828: Creators can refine tracks with natural language edits, which VidTune expands into new gen

principles.principle: Make the dimensions along which candidates vary explicit before or while generating them.
principles.rationale: Users struggle to articulate what actually differs between outputs without a named, structured axis.
principles.tension: Predefined axes can miss idiosyncratic differences only free-form manual grouping would reveal.
principles.evidence: 3151: generation of dimensions and subsequently the (c2) generation of responses using the dimen; 4916: the user is presented with the most informative decision variable, i.e., one that splits t

principles.principle: Arrange candidates spatially so proximity and location encode similarity along a chosen dimension.
principles.rationale: Users struggle to compare many options via lists alone; spatial proximity lets them sense relatedness at a glance.
principles.tension: Conflicts with letting users manually drag candidates into their own groupings.
principles.evidence: 5828: VidTune’s Music Map arranges generated tracks in a 2D space by audio-embedding similarity; 3151: responses (2) reposition to vertically align to their dimension values (Romantic, Somber,

principles.principle: Let users manually drag, drop, or regroup candidates into their own custom clusters.
principles.rationale: Automated clustering may not match how a particular user personally categorizes or perceives similarity.
principles.tension: Conflicts with relying on automatic clustering to pick representative candidates.
principles.evidence: 13510: Users can interact with images and clusters by dragging, dropping, and zooming; 15520: she groups code-text-pairs into themes using drag-and-drop interaction

subparadigms.name: Side-by-Side Comparison
subparadigms.definition: This mechanism produces multiple candidate outputs and then establishes explicit point-to-point correspondences between their matching parts, so each element of one candidate is mapped to its counterpart in the others. The comparison surface is a linked or aligned layout—side-by-side panes, interleaved segments, or shared diagrams with highlighted cross-references—where corresponding units are spatially or visually tied together rather than merely co-located.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If matching sub-elements across candidates are explicitly linked, highlighted, or diffed against each other (segment-to-segment, frame-to-frame), it is Aligned correspondence comparison; if candidates are simply displayed together as whole, unlinked units, it is Flat co-present candidate set.

principles.principle: Let users iteratively refine a generated output via direct edits or targeted instructions.
principles.rationale: Users rarely get the desired result on the first try and need control to correct mismatches.
principles.tension: Edits break the fixed correspondence that aligned comparison views depend on.
principles.evidence: 11792: Alice simply clicked on "Audi-A3", one of the purple cells corresponding to the Model enti; 4474: users can edit a variation, recom- bine multiple variations, and generate a new variation

principles.principle: Visually link or highlight corresponding matching and differing elements across candidate outputs.
principles.rationale: Humans struggle to manually spot subtle overlaps or differences between similar, lengthy outputs.
principles.tension: Requires stable candidates, conflicting with letting users freely edit and regenerate them.
principles.evidence: 2415: Exact matches makes it easy to identify portions of responses that are matching across mul; 4474: aligning videos and highlighting differences through timelines, transcripts, and video pre

principles.principle: Reveal explanatory or auxiliary detail only when the user explicitly requests it.
principles.rationale: Upfront detail overwhelms users and clutters the comparison before it is actually needed.
principles.tension: Works against showing all candidates and their differences simultaneously by default.
principles.evidence: 16497: The right pane (B) remains empty until the user interacts with an information aids button; 11792: a comprehensive textual explanation on how the entity was derived was presented when Alice

principles.principle: Provide an unmodified baseline or original version alongside the augmented or edited one.
principles.rationale: Users need a stable reference point to judge whether an augmentation actually helped.
principles.tension: Doubles interface content, conflicting with minimizing upfront disclosure.
principles.evidence: 17071: Editor-Green, a minimal "blank page" tool, and Editor-Red, our augmented multimodal tool; 5458: shows only the system’s final decision, with no agent-level visibility

subparadigms.name: Exploring Generated Alternatives
subparadigms.definition: The mechanism expands a decision point into a tree of divergent candidate nodes, where selecting or expanding any node spawns further downstream branches rather than a single fixed set.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: Structure is hierarchical and sequential: nodes have parent-child branch relationships and can be expanded/selected to generate further descendants, unlike Flat co-present candidate set, whose siblings sit as one static, non-expandable batch generated in a single pass.

principles.principle: Offer multiple selectable modes giving users different degrees of control over generation.
principles.rationale: Users vary in how much oversight or automation they want over generation.
principles.tension: Adds upfront interface complexity and choice overhead before exploration begins.
principles.evidence: 10017: We compared two interfaces for creating music with an autoregressive generative model: the; 6242: the LLM elicits elaboration through suggestions or questions

P3.name: Context-Aware Proactive Assistance
P3.definition: The interface monitors ambient context, elapsed time, or accumulated signal rather than waiting for an explicit user query, and the system itself decides whether and when to surface a minimal suggestion, reminder, clarification, or disclosure. Initiative for the

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Fuse several sensed channels into one context record before deciding to act, rather than triggering on a single signal.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Any one signal is ambiguous about what the person is doing, and a wrong reading costs an unrequested interruption.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Each added channel raises sensing burden and the surface for false triggers.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Classify the sensed situation into an explicit intermediate state before choosing an action.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Mapping sensors straight to output leaves nothing to inspect when the system intervenes at the wrong moment.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: A fixed state vocabulary is auditable but cannot name situations the designer did not foresee.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Match the intervention's intrusiveness to the user's current activity; default to the quietest channel that can carry it.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Proactive help arrives while the user is mid-task, so the interruption cost is paid before its value is known.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Quiet channels are ignorable — the help arrives and is missed.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 13772: The timing predictor evaluates each message based on its predicted relevance and importanc; 4123: Decreasing the amount of time that the proactive assistant waits to provide suggestions me

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Leave a way out of every proactive act: dismiss, revert, or switch the assistance off.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: The user did not ask, so the system must assume it read the moment wrongly and make that cheap to undo.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Opt-outs preserve autonomy and let the user disable the very help the system was built to give.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Surface the inference as an accept-or-ignore proposal rather than applying it, so a wrong read costs nothing.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Acting on a misread intent forces the user to detect and repair work they never requested.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Confirming every inference reintroduces the interaction cost proactivity was meant to remove.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Pair each proactive act with its rationale or source so the user can judge it without re-deriving the context.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: An unexplained suggestion arriving unbidden gives the user no basis to accept it except deference.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Rationales lengthen a message whose value depended on being glanceable.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Mark AI-originated content and AI activity as visually distinct from the user's own work and the native interface.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: When the system contributes unprompted, users lose track of which parts of the artifact they authored.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Distinct marking preserves authorship attribution but keeps the assistance visibly foreign to the tool.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 4248: presence indicators and interaction context support alleviated disruptions and improved us; 4105: displaying the AI assistant as an animated extra mouse pointer (in green) alongside the us

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Ground the surfaced content in a curated or retrieved domain source rather than the model's own memory.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Unsolicited advice is checked less than advice that was asked for, so its correctness has to be built in.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Curated sources bound correctness and cap the situations the system can speak to.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 13713: DataScout provides query reformulation suggestions to bridge the gap between the user’s qu; 13807: it then uses retrieval-augmented-generation to extract relevant non-visual workarounds fro

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Deliver the assistance inside the tool the user is already working in, in one consistent place.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Help that requires leaving the workflow is not taken up at the moment it was triggered for.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Embedding constrains the interface real estate and inherits the host tool's limits.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 16763: MakeAloud makes the captured data and feedback accessible to the designer within their CAD; 5427: We displayed suggestions in a floating right-hand panel to minimize interruptions to the w

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Keep a user-initiated route to the same assistance the system offers unprompted.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Detection misses moments the user knows about; without a manual route the help exists but cannot be summoned.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: A manual route makes the proactive trigger optional, so its failures go unmeasured.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: When eyes and hands are committed to the physical task, deliver the intervention through audio alone.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Assistance that requires looking at a screen competes with the activity it was triggered to support.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: Audio-only delivery frees attention but leaves nothing persistent to re-read.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Bound the autonomously chosen action to a predefined taxonomy instead of letting the model name its own move.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: An unbounded action space means the user cannot anticipate what the system might do next on their behalf.
paradigm_level_principles.tension: A fixed taxonomy makes behaviour predictable and blocks the response no category covers.

subparadigms.name: Proactive Suggestions
subparadigms.definition: A trigger condition is evaluated once and, upon being met, the system emits exactly one fixed-intensity suggestion, alert, or prompt into the interface. The primary task or conversation continues unimpeded regardless of whether the user notices, accepts, or ignores it, with no escalation, repetition, or autonomous enactment involved.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: Does the emitted item block/pause the system's own ongoing output or task progress until the user resolves it? If yes, withhold_clarify; if the primary task/flow continues regardless and the prompt can simply be ignored, single_tier_surface.

principles.principle: Build a persistent user or knowledge model from ongoing interaction and drive triggers from it, not the momentary signal alone.
principles.rationale: A single surfacing tier has one chance to be relevant; relevance has to come from history the user never restates.
principles.tension: Accumulated models personalize well and make the system's behaviour harder for the user to predict.
principles.evidence: 13623: InterQuest dynamically constructs User-Centric knowledge—cross-task, persistent attributes; 10248: driving behavioral data is analyzed using an assessment metric, in which skill strengths a

principles.principle: Keep continuously sensed personal content on the device: send derived features, not the raw stream.
principles.rationale: Always-on sensing to catch the right moment means the system holds material the user never chose to share.
principles.tension: Local-only processing limits model capability exactly where the sensing is richest.
principles.evidence: 9590: A Flask backend processes conversations entirely on-device to ex- tract statistical signal; 8078: The LLM-based detector, operating on the user’s phone, serves as the protective mechanism

subparadigms.name: Automatic Execution
subparadigms.definition: A detected signal causes the system to directly generate, place, modify, or actuate the artifact or effect itself, committing the change into the shared content, interface, or physical state. No accept/decline step separates detection from enactment, so what the user perceives is the completed result rather than a proposal awaiting confirmation.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: Is the observed output already the enacted change to content/UI/physical state (edit made, object moved, effect actuated) with no accept/decline step, or is it a suggestion/alert the user must still act on to take effect? Enacted→autonomous_execution; presented-only→single_tier_surface.

principles.principle: Narrate the unrequested action as it happens: announce the step, acknowledge the request, confirm the outcome.
principles.rationale: The user did not initiate the act, so without narration they discover its effects only by noticing them later.
principles.tension: Narrating every step becomes the interruption the automation was meant to remove.

principles.principle: Make what the system produced without asking editable and reversible after the fact.

subparadigms.definition: Classifies the user's utterance, intent, or an inferred psychological/task state from existing input and uses that classification to select which of several distinct downstream branches, agents, or response nodes handles the next turn. subparadigms.definition: The pipeline advances an artifact through two or more distinct, fixed-order editable representations, with each stage transforming the prior stage's content into a qualitatively different downstream artifact (e.g., outline → draft → polished output). subparadigms.name: Editing a Generated Draft

subparadigms.name: Persistent Structured Representation
subparadigms.definition: A single canonical structured object—graph, tree, scene, or program—persists as the sole editable state across the interaction rather than being discarded and replaced by a new representation type at each step. subparadigms.name: Embedding Projection

It belongs to this sub-paradigm rather than the parent generally because the spatial coordinate itself is the derived analytic signal (via projection, embedding distance, or scoring), not merely a layout channel for organizing pre-categorized or hierarchical data.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If the visualization's spatial arrangement is produced by a similarity/distance computation (embedding projection, clustering, or a scored axis) such that position itself encodes closeness or score, code Similarity-Based Spatial Positioning; if instead entities are connected by explicit, individually meaningful edges (relationships, flows, or links between named nodes) that the user traverses, code Relational Graph/Flow Linkage.

subparadigms.name: Object-Anchored Overlay
subparadigms.definition: The generated content is bound to a DISCRETE tracked target — a recognized object, marker, prop, instrument, poster, or an individual person's face/body — and its pose determines where the content sits. Moving the target moves the content.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: vs S2 (Scene-geometry conditioned field regeneration): ask what the content would follow if it moved. In S1 there is a nameable discrete target — a recognized object, marker, prop, instrument, poster, or one person's face/body — whose pose the content follows; remove that target and the overlay has nowhere to go. In S2 no single target owns the content: it is conditioned on room mesh, depth map, captured view, or the whole passthrough frame. vs S3: in S1 the target is external to the user and need not be doing anything; in S3 the anchor is the user's own ongoing production.

subparadigms.name: Spatially-Aware Generation
subparadigms.definition: The generated content is conditioned on the RECONSTRUCTED GEOMETRY OR CONTENT OF THE WHOLE SCENE — room mesh, depth map, captured view, walkable bounds, passthrough frame — and fills the ambient field rather than sitting on one target. Changing where you are or what the scene looks like changes what is generated.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: vs S1: if the system reconstructs or captures the environment as a whole (mesh, depth, panorama, passthrough frame, walkable bounds) and generation is conditioned on that reconstruction, it is S2 even when the result visually lands on particular surfaces. If a specific detected object is the addressable unit, it is S1. vs S3: S2 regenerates on viewpoint/scene change; S3 regenerates on each increment of the user's physical act.

subparadigms.name: Embodied Interaction

subparadigms.definition: A detector — a classifier, pattern matcher, or comparison against reference behavior — identifies the exact span, region, line, or stroke within the generated artifact that is problematic, and the interface renders a persistent visual marker anchored to that specific location. subparadigms.name: Criteria-Based Verification
subparadigms.definition: Compares the generated artifact against an explicit external referent — an expert label, a user-authored rubric or criteria set, a checklist, a test suite, a linter, or prior production output — and surfaces the per-item or per-criterion result of that comparison as structured feedback the user can drill into. The verdict's authority comes from the referent, not from the model's own confidence in itself.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: Against its nearest sibling Span-Level Error Localization: ask what the judgment is anchored to. If the system states an external standard it checks against (rubric, expert/gold label, checklist, test cases, a diff against a reference run) and reports outcomes per criterion or per item, code here. If the system merely detects and highlights a problem region inside the content without naming an external standard it compared to, code Span-Level. Against Whole-Response Confidence: this sub-paradigm yields multiple itemised verdicts; that one yields a single aggregate score for the whole output.

subparadigms.name: Confidence Gating
subparadigms.definition: A computed score or check outcome is compared against a threshold, and the result directly changes what the system does next — filtering which suggestions render, gating whether output passes without human review, or triggering an automated repair routine. The check's output is consumed by system logic to alter behavior, rather than existing primarily for a human to read and interpret.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: Distinguish from 'Reference-Based Judgment with Structured Drilldown Feedback': here the check outcome silently changes system routing or rendering (suppress, filter, auto-repair, admit without review); if the outcome is instead packaged as inspectable comparative content for a person to read and reason about, it belongs to the drilldown-feedback cluster.

principles.principle: Route only the lowest-scoring or flagged subset to human review or repair instead of reviewing every output.
principles.rationale: Reviewers have limited attention; making them examine everything wastes it on cases already known to be fine.
principles.tension: Unflagged high-scoring outputs may still contain errors that never reach a human.
principles.evidence: 2477: Human annotators re-annotate instances with lowest verifier scores.; 4871: enabling researchers to prioritise attention and reduce unnecessary intervention

principles.principle: Set the routing/repair threshold by empirically trading measured accuracy gain against review or intervention cost, not a fixed cutoff.
principles.rationale: An arbitrary cutoff either overwhelms reviewers with false alarms or lets real errors through silently.
principles.tension: Empirical tuning per deployment conflicts with letting the end user set their own sensitivity.
principles.evidence: 14541: we offer design implications for which model should be selected by practitioners between h; 2477: Accuracy of the entire dataset after re-annotation vs. total annotation cost.

principles.principle: Condition downstream generation (response options, explanations, rationale) on the upstream classification result rather than producing it independently.
principles.rationale: Generating full output before knowing the risk or category wastes effort and can present irrelevant or unsafe content.
principles.tension: Makes the whole pipeline dependent on one upstream classifier's correctness.

P14.name: Conversational Query over Summaries
P14.definition: The interface generates a condensed summary or narration of a longer source record and layers a free-form chat/QA control on top of it, so the summary itself becomes queryable rather than being the terminal output. Users can interrupt,

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Ground every generated answer in an assembled or retrieved context (session history, summary block, or nearest passages) rather than general knowledge.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Both mechanisms exist to prevent generic or fabricated answers by forcing grounding in specific contextual/retrieved evidence.

paradigm_level_principles.principle: Link generated summaries or answers back to the exact underlying source passage or location so users can verify claims.
paradigm_level_principles.rationale: Both demand surfacing traceable source evidence alongside condensed or synthesized output to prevent blind trust.
paradigm_level_principles.evidence: 6023: CHOIR maintains an embedding index over the documentation repository and performs retrieva; 8343: instructs the LLM to cite specific speaker turn IDs in its generated analysis

subparadigms.name: Anchor-Scoped Query Grounding
subparadigms.definition: A specific point, span, or node in the rendered summary — set by an explicit user click, touch, gesture, or selection, or by a system-generated cluster/link/branching-question structure — fixes the scope that a follow-up query, chat thread, or drill-down view is grounded in, so the user interrogates or navigates to that specific part of the underlying record. It is this sub-paradigm rather than the parent generally because the grounding scope is always tied to a discrete addressable anchor in the rendered summary itself, not to a similarity match over an index or the whole condensed text fed into context.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If the paper describes the query scope as fixed by a user- or system-designated point/link/node already present in the rendered summary (a click, timestamp, cluster, highlighted line), code Anchor-Scoped Query Grounding; if instead the scope is determined at query time by similarity search or routing over a chunk/passage index with no fixed anchor in the display, code Embedding Retrieval Grounding.

principles.principle: Let an explicit user or system action on a specific anchor (click, touch, right-click, node) open a query/chat scoped only to that anchor
principles.rationale: Users need to interrogate one part of a large record without formulating a query that covers the whole thing
principles.tension: Fragments interaction into many narrow scopes, competing with a persistent global overview (see overview principle)
principles.evidence: 15714: Users can explore claims through a chatbot interface (B) by right-clicking and selecting "; 8096: Users can explore criteria via a Criteria Chat (Figure 1 right) or use a General Chat

principles.principle: Pair anchor-level drill-down with a persistent global overview so users retain the whole structure while inspecting one part
principles.rationale: Deep-diving into one anchor risks losing sight of the larger document or dataset it came from
principles.tension: Maintaining an always-visible overview competes for attention and screen space with focused anchor-scoped exploration
principles.evidence: 2030: Present a holistic view of the collective arguments and facilitate the digestion process; 2436: provides users with a comprehensive overview of the information space in the sidebar

principles.principle: Generate system-suggested follow-up questions or sub-goals anchored to the user's current context rather than leaving query formulation to the user
principles.rationale: Users, especially novices, often don't know what to ask next about a given anchor
principles.tension: Over-scaffolding with suggested questions can crowd out open-ended, user-initiated anchor selection
principles.evidence: 2436: Selenite dynamically summarizes users’ progress and suggests avenues for finding additiona; 8256: Explanations accompany the questions to show relevance.

subparadigms.name: Chat-Based Interaction
subparadigms.definition: A generated summary, narrative, or description — sometimes layered into multiple condensation tiers or paired with injected prior-turn/transcript context — is loaded wholesale into the LLM's context window, and the chat layer answers or converses directly over that fixed condensed text. It is this sub-paradigm rather than the parent generally because the entire condensed representation is dumped into context as a single grounding block with no runtime retrieval, matching, or anchor-selection step choosing which part of the source to use.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If the chat/QA turn is grounded on the whole generated summary (or a tier of it selected by gating/progression state) loaded wholesale into context, code Summary-as-Context Chat; if the system instead grounds the turn on a specific point, cluster, link, or node that was set by an explicit user click/selection or a system-generated branching/cluster structure, code Anchor-Scoped Query Grounding.

principles.principle: Transcribe or detect structure from raw audio/video into a compact semantic representation before generating any explanation.
principles.rationale: Raw multimodal streams are too voluminous or unstructured for the LLM or user to process directly.
principles.tension: Compression risks discarding details the grounded response later needs to answer specific questions.
principles.evidence: 15508: Hybrid Frame Sampling and Keyframe Selection for Semantically Efficient Long-Video Represe; 5536: AskNow is listening to the instructor using streaming speech-to-text technology

principles.principle: Give users explicit controls to start, stop, reset, or mute the context capture or assistant output, rather than always-on.
principles.rationale: Continuous transcription or narration can overwhelm, distract, or leak information at the wrong moment.
principles.tension: Pausing capture creates gaps in the very transcript that later responses are grounded on.
principles.evidence: 1524: they can click the circular icon on the top of the chat window; 15510: Start/End Capture button, initiates/stops recording for in-came

principles.principle: Keep the model's presentation of interpretations non-authoritative, letting users correct or override generated meaning rather than asserting conclusions.
principles.rationale: Users need trust that generated summaries won't overwrite their own subjective understanding of source material.
principles.tension: Hedged, editable output feels less decisive than the tiered-depth guidance principle promises.
principles.evidence: 8473: We prompted the GPT to focus on creating a safe, supportive space and avoid interpreting u; 9537: (4) image editing interface and (5) regeneration result

subparadigms.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
subparadigms.definition: An index of chunk, segment, or reasoning-chain embeddings (or a topic-routing table pointing to pre-identified sources) is built over the underlying record, and each incoming query is matched against that index via similarity search or routing to retrieve the specific passages the chat answer is composed from or cites. This makes it a distinct sub-paradigm because grounding is computed fresh per query through a similarity/matching operation over an indexed representation, rather than being fixed by a prior user click, an explicit link structure, or a full-context dump.
subparadigms.boundary_rule: If the paper describes the grounding scope as determined by a similarity/embedding match or topic-routing computation run against an index at query time, code Embedding Retrieval Grounding; if the scope is instead fixed by a user click/selection or a pre-built link/cluster/branching structure in the rendered summary, code Anchor-Scoped Query Grounding.

principles.principle: Route any AI-extracted knowledge, segmentation, or interpretation through human review or confirmation before it becomes trusted index or deployed content.
principles.rationale: Guards against unverified or biased AI interpretations silently becoming canonical grounding material.
principles.tension: Slows the promise of fresh, fully-automatic grounding computed per query.

principles.principle: Shield personal identifiers, filter malicious input, and control model hosting before queries and documents reach the generation step.
principles.rationale: Retrieval pipelines route sensitive user and document content through LLMs, creating privacy exposure and manipulation risk.
principles.tension: Local hosting or heavy filtering can limit access to the most capable external models.

P15.name: Adaptive Interfaces from Inferred User State
P15.definition: The interface continuously infers a user's performance, intent, or physiological state from behavioral or sensor signals and automatically adjusts ongoing layout, difficulty, or content parameters in response. Changes manifest as visible transformations such as reordering, emphasis, or density

subparadigms.name: Context-Aware Adaptation
subparadigms.definition: The interface infers a specific latent variable—recall probability, emotional state, browsing intent, correctness likelihood, confidence/jitter, or task phase—from ongoing behavioral or physiological signals, and uses that inferred value as a direct trigger or parameter for an interface change. The change takes the form of adjusting timing (retrieval triggers, pacing/silence), reordering or adjusting the detail/density of content, switching workflow or recommended elements, or driving visual/physical effects (diffusion, turbulence) and tool/layout selection. The mapping is continuous and one-directional: signal inference feeds forward into a corresponding surface-level parameter change, with no indication of further feedback beyond that adjustment.

principles.principle: Continuously reassess inferred user state throughout the session rather than inferring it once at the start.
principles.rationale: User attention, focus, and physiology drift during a session; a single upfront inference goes stale quickly.
principles.tension: Trades against staged, event-triggered detection that reacts only at discrete phase transitions.
principles.evidence: 10192: observes user behavior and classifies browsing intent at regular intervals; 10247: These HRV metrics are contextualized against individual baseline recordings to account for

principles.principle: Separate raw signal/state inference from the adaptation action via an explicit intermediate representation.
principles.rationale: Coupling noisy inference directly to output makes adaptation unstable and impossible to audit or justify.
principles.tension: Adds pipeline latency and complexity compared to a single end-to-end reactive mapping.
principles.evidence: 9697: this separation is intended to produce more stable and justifiable parameter changes; 10192: adapt existing browsing interfaces in-situ, dynamically adjusting to users' shifting inten

principles.principle: Calibrate inference models to each user's individual baseline before interpreting signals as meaningful.
principles.rationale: Raw physiological or behavioral thresholds vary so much between people that fixed cutoffs misclassify state.
principles.tension: Personalization accuracy competes with minimizing the calibration burden required from new users.
principles.evidence: 10247: These HRV metrics are contextualized against individual baseline recordings to account for; 9838: the system calibrates the user's base- line for gaze and pupil metrics

principles.principle: Give users an explicit way to correct, override, or halt automated adaptation decisions.
principles.rationale: Inference from indirect signals will sometimes misjudge intent or context, and errors erode trust.
principles.tension: Undercuts full automation and adds interruption points the adaptive loop is trying to avoid.
principles.evidence: 7490: the automated system mainly allows humans to abort the machine's; 15898: the system preserves explicit user constraints, keeps user-prioritized metrics in prominen

principles.principle: Detect discrete transitions in inferred state (phase, tier, mode) and switch behavior at those boundaries.
principles.rationale: Continuous experiences move through qualitatively different stages that need different support, not one blended response.
principles.tension: Discrete switching can feel abrupt compared to smooth, graduated adaptation of output parameters.
principles.evidence: 9838: it interprets hesitation levels on a low–medium–high scale using a composite of gaze fix- ; 16313: Upon recognition of a phase transition, CoExplorer notifies users and modifies the display

principles.principle: Adapt output timing and pacing to inferred cognitive or emotional load rather than a fixed schedule.
principles.rationale: Fixed delivery speed ignores that comprehension and readiness to continue vary moment to moment.
principles.tension: Variable pacing can feel unpredictable next to a stable, learnable interaction rhythm.
principles.evidence: 13779: content with high cognitive load is streamed at a lower speed to give users more time to p; 9838: the system slows down or mirrors emotional moments when hesitation increases

principles.principle: Map inferred severity or uncertainty onto continuous, graduated changes in output rather than discrete alerts.
principles.rationale: Explicit warnings interrupt immersion or trust; graded cues convey state without breaking flow.
principles.tension: Graduated cues are subtler but less immediately actionable than a clear discrete alert or tier.

F1.definition: The person holds a goal that is clear to them but cannot state it precisely or completely enough for the system to act on it. This is the gulf of envisioning: specification is incremental and partly unknowable in advance, so the person must externalise a fuzzy intention before any output is possible.

F2.old_analyst_name: Exploring and steering toward the output you want

F3.name: Verification
F3.old_analyst_name: Checking whether an output is right
F3.definition: The person must establish whether a specific output is correct or grounded before acting on it, and verification can cost as much as doing the work unaided. The difficulty is the labour and traceability of verification, not the model's error rate.
F3.boundary_rule: Concerns one output's correctness; F4 concerns visibility into the process that produced it, regardless of whether any output is wrong. Nearest sibling: F4 (Seeing what the system is doing).

F4.name: Transparency
F4.old_analyst_name: Seeing what the system is doing
F4.definition: The person cannot see what the system did, is doing, or is about to do across its steps, so cannot supervise it, intervene mid-course, or form a working model of it. The difficulty is the lack of transparency into the process, and it persists even when every output happens to be correct.

F5.name: Overreliance
F5.old_analyst_name: Knowing how much to rely on it, and staying engaged
F5.definition: The person cannot gauge how much of their judgment to hand over, and hands over more than they intended, so their own scrutiny and effort erode. Overreliance is a standing disposition toward the system rather than a judgment about any one output.
F5.boundary_rule: Concerns global reliance and effort; F3 concerns the act of checking one specific output. Nearest sibling: F3 (Checking whether an output is right).

F6.name: Sensemaking
F6.old_analyst_name: Making sense of more material than one can hold
F6.definition: The person faces more content than they can read, remember, or traverse, and cannot locate, condense, or connect it into something they can act on. The difficulty is sensemaking over volume itself, independent of whether the material is trustworthy.
F6.boundary_rule: Is about comprehending a mass of material; F3 is about validating a claim drawn from it. Nearest sibling: F3 (Checking whether an output is right).

F7.definition: The person loses their place when work spans tools, sessions, or people, and cannot tell when the system should act unprompted, wait, or hand back. The difficulty is mixed-initiative interaction: the timing and division of initiative across a continuing activity.

F8.name: Metacognition
F8.old_analyst_name: Noticing gaps in one's own thinking
F8.definition: The person cannot see flaws, biases, or blind spots in their own reasoning or work without an external mirror, and does not notice when they should stop and check. The gap is metacognitive — in self-monitoring — so it cannot be closed by giving the person more information.
F8.boundary_rule: Is about not knowing that something is wrong; F9 is about knowing it is and not knowing what to change. Nearest sibling: F9 (Knowing what to improve in one's own work).

F9.old_analyst_name: Knowing what to improve in one's own work

F10.name: Rehearsal
F10.definition: The person faces a high-stakes or unfamiliar performance with no low-consequence place to rehearse it and no feedback while rehearsing. The difficulty is the absence of a consequence-free setting for rehearsal, not a lack of instruction.

F12.old_analyst_name: Anticipating how it lands for someone else
F12.definition: The person cannot predict how another specific person will perceive, react to, or need something, so misjudges what to make for them. The difficulty is a limit on perspective-taking toward a particular other.

F13.name: Personalization
F13.old_analyst_name: Generic material that does not land
F13.definition: Content or interaction pitched at no one in particular fails to connect with this person's situation, identity, or goals, and they disengage over time. The difficulty is the absence of personalization, and it is felt as drop-off rather than as error.

F14.name: Accessibility
F14.old_analyst_name: Content locked in an unusable channel
F14.definition: Information arrives in, or must be produced in, a modality this person cannot perceive or operate, so it is unreachable without translation into another channel. The difficulty is accessibility of the channel, which concentrates in but is not defined by particular populations.

F15.name: Spatial grounding
F15.definition: The person must tie language, generated content, or an abstract representation to a particular place, object, or bodily movement, and that correspondence is not given. The difficulty is spatial grounding — the translation between symbolic and spatial form.

F16.name: Participation
F16.definition: In a live shared activity participation goes lopsided, disagreement stays unresolved, and no one manages turns or surfaces quiet contributions. The difficulty is the missing structure of the exchange, not the absence of participants.

F17.name: Privacy and ownership
F17.old_analyst_name: Whose it is, and what is exposed
F17.definition: The person cannot tell or control what of theirs is visible to others — privacy of personal data and likeness on one side, ownership of their own contribution to a joint artifact on the other. Both are a loss of control over how the person is represented to others.

cross_cutting_patterns.name: Model output rendered as annotation anchored to spans of a user artifact
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The system tags specific spans or regions of an artifact the user already has — their code, their essay, a chart, a page, a UI — with generated metadata that stays attached to that exact location. The user reveals it by hovering, clicking, or toggling, rather than reading it in a separate response panel. The base artifact remains the primary object; the generation is a layer on top of it.

cross_cutting_patterns.name: System-posed questions collected as generation parameters
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: Before or between generation steps the system poses concrete questions, form fields, or multiple-choice items to the user, and the answers are used directly as conditioning input for the next generation. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Unstructured artifact deconstructed into an addressable structure first
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: Before generating anything for the user, the system parses a document, chart, video, or image the user supplied into an explicit machine-readable structure — data table, entity-relation set, chapter/step hierarchy, feature set — and every later generation is conditioned on and addressed against that structure. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Generated output voiced as a persistent simulated character
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The system assigns the generation a stable non-assistant identity — a persona, a stakeholder, an object, an animal, a simulated reader or audience — and maintains that identity's context across turns. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Pointing at a target substitutes for describing it in the prompt
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The user indicates a referent by acting on it directly — tapping, lassoing, brushing, gaze, gesture, dragging an element into the query — and the system resolves that deictic act into the reference the model needs. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Explicit numeric score or uncertainty rendered beside output
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The system computes a confidence, calibration, severity, probability, or per-trait score and renders it as a separate display element attached to a specific output, distinct from the output's content. cross_cutting_patterns.definition: Candidate or past generations are placed in a durable spatial structure — grid, palette, 2D axes, cluster map, scatter of glyphs — where position encodes an attribute such as time, topic, region, or a rated dimension. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Model pre-fills a criterion-keyed judgment the user adjudicates item by item
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The system populates a structured judgment against predefined criteria — rubric rows, codebook categories, screening decisions, per-criterion ratings — and renders it as an editable list, table, or matrix. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Continuously sampled non-linguistic signal conditions the next generation
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: A sensor stream — gaze, heart rate, EEG, prosody, touch, force, camera — is sampled continuously and fused into a state the model reads on each turn, so output shifts without the user issuing a matching command. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Two artifacts placed together with computed discrepancies marked
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The interface shows two artifacts — user draft against model reference, two model outputs, two versions, expected against actual — and computes and marks exactly where they differ, often after decomposing both into comparable units such as claims or cells. cross_cutting_patterns.definition: Generations are held in a tree where any node can spawn multiple candidate children; the user branches, prunes, or collapses, and further generation is conditioned only on the chosen node's ancestry while sibling branches remain viewable and returnable. cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The user draws — a squiggle, a stroke over a video frame, a 3D curve, a mask, a sketch of a scene — and the system interprets that mark as a spatial or intentional specification the model generates from. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Continuous control bound to a model-side parameter recomputes output
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: A slider, weight, threshold, fader, or numeric bound is wired directly to a parameter the system uses to score, filter, blend, or clamp generation, and moving it recomputes output with no new typed instruction. cross_cutting_patterns.name: Bounded region selection scopes regeneration to that region
cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The user marks a bounded area of an image, frame, or canvas by brushing, masking, lassoing, or clicking, and the system segments it, binds it to a semantic label or prompt fragment, and regenerates only that area while the rest is preserved. cross_cutting_patterns.definition: The system maintains an explicit internal representation of the user's intent, preference, knowledge, or working state — a belief distribution, evidence graph with trust states, accumulated domain-knowledge store, working-state vector — and updates it across turns or sessions.
